bull.argument: The filing describes a company with deep strategic assets and clear growth vectors. Online advertising, though over 70% of 2025 revenues, is being reshaped by AI, and management frames AI as a driver of usage: it states that user engagement with AI products "will continue to benefit our business and our revenues." Revenues beyond advertising are a growing share: "Certain of these revenues have been growing at a rate higher than our advertising revenues, becoming a larger percentage of our consolidated revenues, and we expect this trend to continue." Management is also investing heavily in its own infrastructure, including custom TPUs, with the expectation that its technical infrastructure investment will "significantly increase" in 2026, and it notes it expects "to continue to drive efficiencies in our data centers." The risks are real. Antitrust remedies could be structural, and margins may compress as mix shifts to lower-margin businesses. But the filing shows a company investing from a position of scale, with diversified revenue streams and a demonstrated ability to grow. The bull case rests on that scale converting heavy investment into durable returns.

claims.claim: Management expects AI user engagement to benefit revenues
claims.quote: We expect that this evolution, including user engagement with AI products and services, will continue to benefit our business and our revenues.

claims.claim: Non-advertising revenues are growing faster and gaining share
claims.quote: Certain of these revenues have been growing at a rate higher than our advertising revenues, becoming a larger percentage of our consolidated revenues, and we expect this trend to continue.

claims.claim: Management expects efficiencies in data centers to continue despite rising infrastructure costs
claims.quote: While our technical infrastructure costs increase, we expect to continue to drive efficiencies in our data centers

bear.argument: The filing presents a company whose largest risks are both concentrated and rising. More than 70% of 2025 revenues came from online advertising, and management concedes that AI is 'quickly reshaping the advertising industry' and that 'there is no assurance that we will adapt effectively.' Meanwhile, the company expects its technical infrastructure investment to 'significantly increase' in 2026, with costs that are 'expected to significantly increase,' and it warns that some costs 'are relatively fixed and may not correlate to changes in revenue.' Margins are under explicit pressure: management says it 'may experience downward pressure on our operating margin' and that the faster-growing non-ad revenues carry margins that 'are generally lower than the margins on our advertising revenues.' The bull's point that growth beyond advertising is rising is true, but the filing says that growth dilutes margins. On top of this, the filing describes an antitrust case where the DOJ's remedy proposal 'includes structural remedies that could harm our business,' and states the company may have to 'divest' parts of its business. Investors are being asked to fund very large, long-duration commitments with no assurance of return.

claims.claim: Advertising concentration plus AI disruption creates adaptation risk
claims.quote: We believe AI is quickly reshaping the advertising industry, including how ads are delivered online, and we and our competitors are constantly adjusting to meet this shift

claims.claim: Infrastructure spending and costs are set to rise sharply
claims.quote: The costs associated with operating our technical infrastructure - depreciation, energy, equipment, and network capacity - are expected to significantly increase

claims.claim: Management warns of margin pressure from lower-margin mix
claims.quote: The margins on these revenues vary significantly and are generally lower than the margins on our advertising revenues.

bull.argument: The opponent is right that margins and risks are real, but the filing does not show a company losing its footing. Management's own risk language calls AI a shift the company is actively adapting to, and it says AI engagement "will continue to benefit our business and our revenues." The margin point cuts both ways: the filing says non-ad revenues carry lower margins, yet it also says those revenues are "growing at a rate higher than our advertising revenues." Lower-margin growth still adds absolute profit, and the filing does not say it erodes the advertising base. On cost, the filing pairs rising infrastructure spend with a stated intent to "continue to drive efficiencies in our data centers," which is the mitigation the opponent omits. On antitrust, the filing says the remedies "range... varies widely" and that the company "plan[s] to appeal" the adverse portion of the decision, so structural outcomes are possible but not settled. The honest bull case is that scale and diversification give management room to absorb these pressures, while the risks are concentrated enough to warrant close monitoring.

claims.claim: Management expects AI engagement to benefit revenues, countering the opponent's adaptation concern
claims.quote: We expect that this evolution, including user engagement with AI products and services, will continue to benefit our business and our revenues.

claims.claim: Non-ad revenue growth is outpacing advertising, the mix shift the opponent calls margin dilution
claims.quote: Certain of these revenues have been growing at a rate higher than our advertising revenues, becoming a larger percentage of our consolidated revenues, and we expect this trend to continue.

claims.claim: Management plans efficiency gains to offset rising infrastructure costs
claims.quote: While our technical infrastructure costs increase, we expect to continue to drive efficiencies in our data centers

bear.argument: The bull concedes the risks but leans on two points the filing does not support. First, 'continue to drive efficiencies' is stated as an intent, not a result, and the filing immediately qualifies it: 'we may also not be able to continue to drive efficiencies at the rate we have in the past,' while also warning that 'Certain of our costs and expenses are relatively fixed and may not correlate to changes in revenue.' Second, the claim that lower-margin growth 'still adds absolute profit' is not in the filing; what it says is that margins 'may continue to have, an adverse effect on our consolidated margins.' Pairing faster non-ad growth with lower margins means the mix shift can dilute the company's overall profitability even as revenue rises. On AI, the filing's own words are that 'there is no assurance that we will adapt effectively and competitively.' Management's engagement claim is a hope; the risk factor is the disclosure. On antitrust, the DOJ remedy proposal 'includes structural remedies that could harm our business,' and the filing confirms the search judgment already 'imposes restrictions on how we distribute our services.' Those are realized constraints, not hypotheticals. Scale is a reason the company can absorb losses, but the filing does not show that the returns on its rising capital commitments are assured.

claims.claim: Management itself doubts it can keep driving efficiencies at past rates
claims.quote: we may also not be able to continue to drive efficiencies at the rate we have in the past

claims.claim: Mix shift toward lower-margin businesses may hurt consolidated margins
claims.quote: margins on our devices have had, and may continue to have, an adverse effect on our consolidated margins

claims.claim: The search remedies already restrict how the company distributes its services
claims.quote: imposes restrictions on how we distribute our services and requires us to share certain search data

judge.reasoning: All quotes in both rounds are verified, but the bear built its case on more specific, directly relevant disclosures (margin dilution, fixed costs, realized search restrictions) and rebutted the bull's efficiency and absolute-profit claims with filing language. The bull's rebuttal asserted that lower-margin growth 'still adds absolute profit' without filing support, and it relied on management intentions ('expect to continue to drive efficiencies') that the bear effectively qualified.
